To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of lipids to a corn-soy-based diet improved nutrient and energy digestibilities in young pigs and that the type of lipid source used affected nutrient and energy digestiblities, but the peroxidation level of lipids did not.

the lipid source (CN or CA versus PF or TL) affected nutrient and energy digestible values of the diets, and the lipid peroxidation had no detectable influence on nutrient and energy digestion in pigs.
the addition of lipids to the diet increased ATTD of GE, EE, and N, and that the type of lipid source affected AT TD of GE, EE and C, and tended to influence DE values.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of lipid source and lipid peroxidation on nutrient and energy values and digestibility of lipids.
the effects of different lipid sources (CN, CA, PF, and TL) and lipid oxidation levels (OL, SO, and ROL) on nutrient and energy utilization in young pigs.
the effects of lipid source and lipid peroxidation on nutrient and energy values of the various lipid sources in young pigs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the DE and ME values for CN and CA were about 450 and 450 kcal/kg, respectively, greater than that of the TL and PF, with PF being intermediate, and the lipid peroxidation did not influence the DE and ME of the lipids.
lipid sources and their peroxidation level have no effect on the DE and ME value of the lipids, but lipid sources do affect ATTD of dietary nutrients and energy.
lipids from vegetable oils are more digestible than lipids from animal fats, and the digestibility values for CN and CA are greater than for PF and TL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lipid source affected the digestibility of DM, GE and EE, while lipid oxidation had no detectable effect on the digestibility of nutrients and energy values of the lipid.

the lipid sources and lipid peroxidation had no significant impact on the ME value of the various lip ids, while lipid source affected AT TD of dietary DM, EE, GE, N, and Ca and tended to affect DE value of the various oils.

the lipid source used in the current study had no detectable effect on the ME value of the lipid and the lipid source and the level of lipid peroxidization had no detectable influence on the ME value.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CN and CA are superior sources of lipid for pigs, and TL is inferior to CN, CA, and PF.
lipid source affects nutrient and energy digestibilty in pigs and lipid peroxidation level did not affect nutrient and energy digestibililty in pigs fed the experimental diets.
the lipid source and lipid oxidation level did not affect the ME value of the lipid, which is in contrast with the results of other studies.
